structured_output.summary: The most useful find is a public submission to this same competition. The repo is RyanChong0117/CIFAR-100-speedrun, whose rules match RULES.md here. The submission (futurebiohackers PR #3) reports 75.29% mean accuracy in 8.11 s of prepare+train. That was over 40 trials on a Modal A100-SXM4-80GB, the same GPU type as this machine. The organizer baseline was a 40-epoch ResNet9 at width 64 (75.36% in 59.3 s). The submission used Keller Jordan's airbench96 network with three blocks of 128, 384 and 512 channels, 3 convs per block, and the last block widened to 576. It trained for 8.5 epochs with plain SGD and no TTA, and used torch.compile plus synthetic warmup in the untimed build. Its sweep found Muon lost to SGD at every size, and 9 epochs gave 75.6% in 8.58 s. Treat ~8 s as the bar to beat, and seed the tree with an airbench96-style recipe, not a ResNet. The airbench96 starting settings are in the hyperparameter finding below. The rules ban TTA, which accounts for 0.45–0.8 pp of airbench's published accuracy, so its CIFAR-10 numbers overstate what is reachable here. Directions nobody has tried on CIFAR-100: airbench96_faster's hard-example data filtering, the whitening/dirac/lookahead/alternating-flip set (measured on CIFAR-10 only), and spending more epochs on a narrower net. Caveats: the PR pages now return 404, so the recipe details come from search-engine snippets and could not be read in full. The airbench ablation speedups were all measured on CIFAR-10.

findings.source: https://github.com/abdullah-athar/iterate-futurebiohackers/pull/3 (PR title and search snippets; the page itself now returns 404)
findings.claim: A CIFAR-100 speedrun submission adapted from airbench reached 75.29% mean accuracy (sd 0.25 pp) in 8.11 s mean prepare+train (sd 0.02 s) over 40 trials on a Modal A100-SXM4-80GB. Recipe: airbench96 net (128/384/512, 3 convs per group) with the last block widened to 576, 8.5 epochs, no TTA. torch.compile and synthetic warmup ran in the untimed build; GPU transfer, normalization and whitening init ran in the timed prepare. In the same sweep, 9 epochs with last block 576 gave 75.6% in 8.58 s. The organizer baseline (ResNet9, width 64, 40 epochs) scored 75.36% in 59.30 s.
findings.relevance: This is the same benchmark, rules and GPU type as the task. It sets the time to beat (~8.1 s) and shows an airbench96-family net at ~8.5 epochs sits right at the 75% edge. Its 0.25 pp sd across seeds means our 0.753 margin over 3 seeds is tight at 75.3–75.5% means.
hypotheses: Lvl1 candidate: architecture/throughput trade-off (airbench-style whitened CNN) dominates time-to-75%
Lvl3 candidate: airbench96 128/384/576, 8.5 ep, SGD reproduces >=0.753 at ~8 s on this machine

findings.claim: In the futurebiohackers sweep, 'Muon lost to SGD at every size', so they removed it from the final recipe.
findings.relevance: Evidence against swapping the airbench96 Nesterov SGD for Muon on CIFAR-100, even though Muon set the CIFAR-10 94% record (2.59 s).
hypotheses: Optimizer hypothesis: Muon for conv filters reduces epochs-to-75% on CIFAR-100 (prior evidence refutes it)

findings.claim: Evaluation is one view per image: no TTA, no test-set statistics, no state changes. Untimed build may compile, autotune, capture CUDA graphs and warm up on synthetic inputs, but all such state must be reset. Timed work includes GPU transfer, casting, preprocessing including whitening, augmentation and fitting. Nondeterministic CUDA kernels and custom Triton/CUDA are allowed. The official GPU is the A100 80GB PCIe (300 W), so times will run slower than on SXM.
findings.relevance: TTA, the source of a large part of airbench's published accuracy, is banned. CUDA-graph capture in build is explicitly allowed, which matters for a ~8 s run made of many small steps. Whitening init counts toward the score, so it should be fast, e.g. computed on a subset of patches.
hypotheses: Overhead hypothesis: CUDA graphs / compile max-autotune in build cut per-step overhead at small batch
Whitening-init cost hypothesis: computing PCA on a patch subset saves prepare time with no accuracy loss

findings.claim: With CIFAR-10 hyperparameters left untuned, airbench96 (40 epochs, 12-px Cutout, TTA) reached 79.27% on CIFAR-100 without Cutout and 79.76% with Cutout, versus 77.54% and 78.04% for ResNet-18. On CIFAR-10, TTA adds +0.81 pp for airbench94 (93.2 to 94.01) and +0.45 pp for airbench96.
findings.relevance: The airbench96 family has ~4.5 pp of headroom over 75% on CIFAR-100 at 40 epochs, so the budget can be cut ~4–5x. TTA is banned here, so expect roughly 0.5–1 pp lower accuracy than the published TTA numbers at equal epochs.
hypotheses: Epoch-budget hypothesis: accuracy vs epochs curve for airbench96 on CIFAR-100 crosses 75.3% near 8-9 epochs without TTA

findings.claim: Epochs needed for 94% on CIFAR-10, applying techniques cumulatively: baseline 45. Frozen patch-whitening init: 21 ('the single most impactful feature'). Dirac/identity init: 18. Scaled BN-bias LR and related optimizer tricks: 13.5. Lookahead: 12.0. Multi-crop TTA: 10.8. Alternating (derandomized) flip: 9.9. Alternating flip alone equals a 27% speedup at 20 epochs without Cutout, 38% at 40 epochs, and 18.6% at 40 epochs with Cutout.
findings.relevance: Ranks which components to check first if a recipe lacks them, and which to ablate for time savings. All numbers are from CIFAR-10, so the CIFAR-100 effect sizes are unverified.
hypotheses: Whitening+dirac init are necessary components (ablating them raises epochs-to-75% substantially)
Alternating flip beats random flip at short budgets on CIFAR-100
Lookahead/EMA gives ~1 epoch saving at short budgets

findings.claim: airbench96 hyperparameters: batch 1024; lr 9.0 per 1024 examples; Nesterov momentum 0.85; weight decay 0.012; BN-bias LR scaler 64; label smoothing 0.2; whitening bias trained for 3 epochs; 10% warmup then linear decay; Lookahead with decay 0.95^5·(t/T)^3. Augmentation: flip, translate 4, cutout 12. Net: widths 128/384/512, 3 convs per group with a residual over the last two, 2x2 whitening conv, output scaling 1/9, 37 epochs.
findings.relevance: Likely starting settings for an 8–9 epoch CIFAR-100 recipe. At this short a budget, Cutout 12 and translate 4 may over-regularize, and label smoothing 0.2 may need retuning for 100 classes. These knobs are untested in the public CIFAR-100 entry.
hypotheses: Regularization hypothesis: at ~8 epochs, removing/reducing Cutout and translate raises accuracy (under-fitting regime)
Label smoothing value (0.1 vs 0.2) shifts accuracy at short budget on CIFAR-100

findings.claim: airbench94_muon reaches 94.01% on CIFAR-10 in 2.59 s on an A100. Net: widths 64/256/256, 2 convs per group, GELU, BN in float32 (momentum 0.6, eps 1e-12, frozen weight), fp16 channels_last model. Batch 2000, 8 epochs, label smoothing 0.2, flip+translate 2, model.compile(mode='max-autotune'), cudnn.benchmark. Muon (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6) on conv filters; SGD on biases (lr 0.053) and head (lr 0.67).
findings.relevance: These engineering details (fp16 channels_last, max-autotune, large batch, BN in fp32) cut per-epoch time, separately from the network itself. A smaller net than airbench96 trained for more epochs may also reach 75% faster.
hypotheses: Throughput hypothesis: fp16/channels_last + max-autotune + batch ~2000 lowers s/epoch without accuracy cost
Width/depth trade-off: a narrower net (e.g. 96/256/384) for more epochs beats 128/384/576 at 8.5 epochs in wall time

findings.claim: airbench96_faster cut the 96% CIFAR-10 time from 34.7 s to 27.3 s (4.9 to 3.1 PFLOPs) with data filtering. A small proxy net (32/64/64, 2 convs per block) scores each batch of 1024, and the main net trains only on the 512 highest-loss examples. Other settings: 45 epochs, cutout 12, translate 4, TTA.
findings.relevance: An approach not yet tried on CIFAR-100: dropping low-loss examples halves backward compute per step. The proxy pass costs time, and in short (~8 epoch) under-fitting runs the gain may shrink or reverse.
hypotheses: Data-filtering hypothesis: proxy-based hard-example selection lowers time-to-75% on CIFAR-100 at short budgets

findings.claim: A 'critical damping' momentum schedule, mu(t) = 1 − 2·sqrt(alpha(t)), reached 90% on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 2.34x faster than constant mu = 0.9. On CIFAR-100, the gain at matched final accuracy shrank to 1.14x.
findings.relevance: Weak evidence that momentum-schedule tricks give only small gains in final-accuracy terms on CIFAR-100. Low priority.
hypotheses: Momentum-schedule hypothesis: scheduling momentum gives <=~10% time saving at matched accuracy

findings.claim: An autonomous multi-agent research loop cut the CIFAR-10 Airbench96 wall-clock by only 4.59%, after 1,197 headline trials.
findings.relevance: An already-optimized airbench recipe leaves little to gain from hyperparameter search alone. Larger savings are likelier from fewer epochs, net size, or skipping work (data filtering, overhead).
hypotheses: Meta: hyperparameter-only tweaks on a tuned airbench base yield <~5% time gains
